title: Voter-Induced Municipal Credit Risk
authors: Brent W. Ambrose; Matthew Gustafson; Maxence Valentin; Ziming Ye
eligible_reason: Single event date with continuous treatment intensity: post = 1 if trade_ym >= 201707 for every bond (Data/Codes/2.Additional_variables.R line 70; TCJA SALT cap), interacted with decrease_itm, the county share of filers who stop itemizing (continuous; binary highchangeded = decrease_itm >= 0.195 used elsewhere). Table 2: felm(spread2_inv_w01 ~ post*decrease_itm [+ county and bond controls] | state_ym + cusip_id | 0 | trade_ym + fips2). One adoption date and a continuous dose, so not a staggered binary design; most columns also add time-varying controls; Table 6 uses entropy balancing weights.
design_notes: R lfe::felm on bond-month municipal GO bond trades (MSRB/Mergent). Bond FE and state x month FE. Tables 3-4 split by voter-approval requirements / border pairs; Table 5 alternative TCJA measures; Table 7 bond issuance with issue_ym + issuer FE. Figure 3 dynamic effects around the same date.
data_files_note: README: 'an anonymized 10% random sample of the true final dataset' with anonymized state, county, issuer and bond identifiers; raw MSRB/Mergent data not shared.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Single TCJA date (July 2017) with continuous exposure; not staggered.
